FL-197.label: Spend and Palace state reads use the calling principal; only the configured owner can request the whole Palace.
FL-197.walk: In a verification daemon, open Spend and Palace State and see only that principal's receipts and counts. In a local fixture, compare the configured owner's whole-Palace view. Request scope=palace as the verification principal and see a plain 403. Keep owner-rack captures out of evidence.
FL-197.observed: This capture shows the current verification app as context. The exact broader walk printed above was not established by this packet; F086 retains that evidence gap. The Jobs change does not convert it into a feature PASS.

FL-169.label: Client and cloud versions stay sync-locked or backward compatible, following industry practice, so version differences feel seamless.
FL-169.walk: Start a client whose version differs from the cloud Palace's; it either keeps working or refuses with a plain version message.
FL-169.observed: The 0.1.25 client completed the real shell conversation while Palace still served 0.1.24, then continued on deployed API 0.1.25/schema 0025 for Jobs. Health, shell and Jobs receipts record both phases.

FL-187.label: Two repos, the spine (memory) and the Harness, not a mono repo.
FL-187.walk: List the repositories; the spine and the Harness are two separate git repos.
FL-187.observed: Harness and Memory remain independent Git repositories and independent PyPI distributions. The release/install receipts and PRs are the proof; the screenshot is current application context.

FL-195.label: The feature ledger generates coverage reports and requires evidence for the rows affected by a build.
FL-195.walk: Compute the composer fix's impact with --paths and see attunement rows; push a branch touching socket.ts and observe the hook print rows and write impacted.json; observe a DONE handoff without screenshots fail CI, then verify complete evidence passes.
FL-195.observed: The push hook printed mapped rows and wrote impacted.json. Garden test_push_writes_impact_and_ci_refuses_only_done_without_evidence passed in the 30-test negative/control suite. Screenshot is application context; the test log proves rejection behavior.

FL-196.label: The rules machine checks citations, frozen law, product vocabulary, seed states and packet precedents.
FL-196.walk: Remove a guard citation on a disposable branch and observe CI fail; change a frozen axiom and observe the freeze step fail; restore both and observe Rules pass. The master ADR check remains red until the owner applies the citation patch.
FL-196.observed: The 30-test Garden suite exercised changed frozen-law bytes and missing guard citations; final canonical/product/rules checks pass after the corrections. Hosted Rules pass. Screenshot is application context, with test/CI logs retained.

FL-162.label: Easy onboarding from a single splash repo, needing only two secrets: a GCP credential and an OpenRouter key.
FL-162.walk: On a fresh machine, follow the splash repo's install steps; you are asked for a GCP credential and an OpenRouter key and nothing else before the app comes up.
FL-162.observed: This capture shows the current verification app as context. The exact broader walk printed above was not established by this packet; F086 retains that evidence gap. The Jobs change does not convert it into a feature PASS.

FL-182.label: Agent workflows that are programmable, so making agents do work is extremely easy.
FL-182.walk: Save an agent workflow and run it twice; both runs do the same work without a person steering.
FL-182.observed: Imported one recipe JSON through Jobs and clicked Run now twice without steering. Both fresh threads wrote the same M3SJ_READY file and passed the frozen exit check. Real Palace/OpenRouter receipts retain identical definitions.

FL-183.label: Agent workflows can be set up on cron jobs.
FL-183.walk: Put a workflow on a cron schedule; it fires at the scheduled time.
FL-183.observed: One-minute UTC cron fired in Jobs, survived daemon restart and fired again. File, queue and Palace revision triggers each completed real OpenRouter work. The Palace trigger first failed on a missing nullable selector; 0.1.26 fixes it and the corrected run passed. All five test definitions are paused.
